draft.title: Synovial joints
card: A synovial joint is a freely moving joint, such as the knee, shoulder, hip or elbow. The bone ends sit inside a capsule that holds the joint together.
Articular cartilage
a smooth, slippery layer on the ends of the bones. It reduces friction and cushions the bones when they meet.
Synovial fluid
a thick liquid inside the capsule. It lubricates the joint, so the bones move easily, and it feeds the cartilage.
Ligaments
tough bands that join bone to bone. They hold the joint steady and limit movements that could cause injury.
draft.remember: Synovial joints move freely because cartilage and fluid cut friction, and ligaments keep the bones in place.

a.q: Which part of a synovial joint reduces friction by lubricating the joint?
a.why: Synovial fluid is the liquid that lubricates the joint so the bones glide. Articular cartilage is the tempting option: it makes a smooth surface and cushions, but the lubricating liquid is the fluid.
a.clue: Think of which part is a liquid.

b.q: Sam lands awkwardly in netball and his knee bends sideways. The bones stay in place because a structure limits the movement. What is it?
opts: Articular cartilage on the bone ends
The smooth surface of the bones
b.why: Ligaments join bone to bone, holding the joint steady and limiting movements that could injure it. Cartilage is tempting because it protects the joint, but it cushions and reduces friction rather than holding bones in place.
b.clue: Which part joins one bone to another?

problems.detail: The clue 'Think of which part is a liquid' gives the answer away. Synovial fluid is the only liquid among the options, so a student can pick it without knowing what each part does.
The clue 'Which part joins one bone to another?' matches the right option's wording 'joining bone to bone', so a student can match the words without understanding what ligaments do.

a.q: Which part of a synovial joint reduces friction by lubricating the joint?
a.why: Synovial fluid lubricates the joint so the bones glide. Articular cartilage is the tempting option: it also reduces friction, but it does this by giving a smooth surface and cushioning, not by lubricating.

b.q: Sam lands awkwardly in netball and his knee bends sideways. The bones stay in place because a structure limits the movement. What is it?
opts: Articular cartilage on the bone ends

b.clue: Which part stops a joint moving further than it should?
